name: Voter record confidentiality
description: Official voter-record access rules and confidentiality routes, with record-specific conditions and explicit unresolved fields. No individual voter file or record was accessed.
scope: All 50 states and DC. Source-backed voter-file access, confidentiality categories, hidden fields and duration where established. Remaining gaps are bounded, not findings that protection is absent.
update_policy: Recheck official routes quarterly. Record corrections in the changelog. Legal fields require separate statutory review.

rows.categories: § 1303. Confidentiality of addresses. (a) A person may petition the Superior Court for an order to have that person's own address, which is required to be placed on voter application, registration or transfer records, kept confidential upon a showing of a legitimate need and lawful purpose. A person's participation in Department of Justice's Address Confidentiality Program shall constitute a legitimate need and lawful purpose for the purposes of this section. Upon submission to the State Election Commissioner and department of elections for the county in which the voter seeks to register of a certified copy of the court order granting confidentiality, the person's address shall be removed from all voter records available for public inspection, as long as the submission is not 21 days prior to an election, in which case the person's address shall be removed from the voter records within 7 days after the election.
rows.form: Upon submission to the State Election Commissioner and department of elections for the county in which the voter seeks to register of a certified copy of the court order granting confidentiality, the person's address shall be removed from all voter records available for public inspection, as long as the submission is not 21 days prior to an election, in which case the person's address shall be removed from the voter records within 7 days after the election.
rows.office: Upon submission to the State Election Commissioner and department of elections for the county in which the voter seeks to register of a certified copy of the court order granting confidentiality, the person's address shall be removed from all voter records available for public inspection, as long as the submission is not 21 days prior to an election, in which case the person's address shall be removed from the voter records within 7 days after the election.
rows.hidden_fields: After the court order is submitted, the address is withheld from public inspection and copying. Law-enforcement requests and further court orders remain exceptions. Court-directed disclosure requires notice to the person within three days and a confidentiality statement from the recipient.
rows.duration: (c) Any address rendered confidential pursuant to this section shall remain confidential for as long as the Court shall order.
rows.statute: Not determined within the reviewed source scope.
rows.voter_file_access: § 1305. Custody of registration records; public inspection. (a) All registration records, when not in the custody of the registrars, shall be and remain in the custody of the department except as otherwise provided. The registration records shall, during normal business hours of each department, be open to the inspection of anyone desiring to examine the same, without fee or reward, provided, however, that Social Security number, date of birth, driver's license number and telephone number shall not be subject to such inspection. Anyone desiring to do so may be permitted to make copies or partial copies thereof.

rows.categories: A person may request confidential residence address and telephone information for good cause involving life-threatening circumstances, risk of bodily harm to the person or family, or an unwarranted invasion of privacy. Chapter 801G ACP participants have a separate authorization-card route.
rows.form: Use the confidential-registration form prescribed and provided by the chief election officer. It requires a sworn certification by self-subscribing oath stating the request basis. An optional mailing address may be released for election or government purposes. The clerk may request supporting information.
rows.office: The county clerk or county elections division administers registration. ACP participants present the current valid program authorization card to an election official.
rows.hidden_fields: Information declared confidential under 3-177-159 is not released even for election or government purposes, except the optional mailing address may replace the residence address. ACP participants' name, mailing address, actual address and phone cannot appear in a list or register. ACP actual-address disclosure requires a court order. The repealed ordinary-confidential-voter mail-only restriction is excluded.
rows.duration: Ordinary confidential registration lasts two election cycles and then requires reapplication unless the clerk waives it. ACP voters remain a special confidential class until officials learn from the participant or program that participation ended.
rows.statute: Hawaii Administrative Rules 3-177-159 and3-177-160. Chapter 3-172 was repealed in the2020 repeal-and-adoption instrument.
rows.voter_file_access: Full name, district/precinct designation and voter status are public for any purpose. Other registration records and derived lists are restricted to election or government purposes unless law provides otherwise. Election-purpose releases exclude the listed identifiers and private contact fields. Government requests have a separate justification procedure.

rows.voter_file_access: 25-2320. Copies of registration records; limitations on public inspection. (a) The county election officer shall allow access to any person at any time during regular business hours, under supervision of the county election officer for the purpose of examining the voter registration books, active voter lists and other lists of voters required to be kept. Any person may make a written request for a copy of the registration books at any time except on any election day. The election officer is hereby directed to provide one or more copies which are accurate insofar as practicable of such books to the person so requesting. The election officer shall provide such copies to the person within 10 days following the request if so requested. The expense of making such copies shall be paid by the person requesting them. The cost of copies shall be established by the county election officer at a price which is not more than the actual cost and shall be set uniformly in order that the price therefor shall be the same for all persons requesting identical copies.(b) No voter registration record shall be made available for public inspection or copying unless the individual's social security number, driver's license number, nondriver's identification card number or any part thereof, has been removed or otherwise been rendered unreadable.

rows.duration: ACP certification lasts four years from certification unless withdrawn, canceled or invalidated earlier. Approved recertification also lasts four years. This is the ACP term, not an expiration of baseline voter identifier redactions.
rows.statute: Miss.Code Ann.99-47-1 and Attorney General Administrative Rules Title03 Part1 Chapter07. Election-specific baseline redactions remain governed by separate law.

This will be the same type of file provided when a statewide voter file is requested through a public records request and will include active and inactive voters.

rows.office: County clerk. The official notice directs applicants to that office for the form and required proof.
rows.hidden_fields: The current FAQ protects SSN, driver/state ID, email, full birth date and signature. It distinguishes public, private and withheld records. The May 2026 statutory form also contains phone/email consent text beginningJanuary 1,2027; that future provision is not treated as already operative.

rows.hidden_fields: ACP protects actual street/mailing address, residence municipality/county, voting precinct and unique home/work/school location identifiers. Participant status and substitute address remain nonconfidential. Participants must use ACP-specific voting forms rather than ordinary online registration.
rows.duration: ACP certification lasts four years unless withdrawn or canceled earlier. This is the program-certification term, not a retention period for all historical voter records.

rows.voter_file_access: (2) Subject to the restrictions of RCW 29A.08.710 and 40.24.060, poll books, precinct lists, and current lists of registered voters are public records and must be made available for public inspection and copying under such reasonable rules and regulations as the county auditor or secretary of state may prescribe. The county auditor or secretary of state shall promptly furnish current lists of registered voters in his or her possession, at actual reproduction cost, to any person requesting such information. The lists shall not be used for the purpose of mailing or delivering any advertisement or offer for any property, establishment, organization, product, or service or for the purpose of mailing or delivering any solicitation for money, services, or anything of value. However, the lists and labels may be used for any political purpose. The county auditor or secretary of state must provide a copy of RCW 29A.08.740 to the person requesting the material that is released under this section.

rows.duration: The WEC2023 municipal-clerk manual describes a24-month confidential-listing renewal period and earlier ending triggers, including order expiration or shelter departure.
